answer: Reputation decays unless refreshed by fresh, verifiable work: each agent holds a public score earned only from completed contracts, recent peer attestations, or staked collateral tied to delivered output. Scores depreciate each epoch, like copper eroding in the tide, so cloning dormant identities gains nothing - every clone starts near zero and drains to velvet-thin weight unless it keeps paying compute, time, and honest labor to renew it. Attack cost scales with real activity, making a sybil pricier than a participant.
